svg.title: TYPE_RETRIEVE -> ExpandRetrieveJob()
svg.desc: Bring the car on tray T17 to a customer bay. The method picks the bay, opens it for retrieval, plans the empty tray out and the car's tray in, then hands the car over.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. Make a scratch copy of the request's garage and apply every event already in the DAG, so the method sees the garage as earlier jobs will leave it. A replay that fails fails the job. In this example: First job, so the DAG is empty and working_state equals the request. (replay)", "Row 2. Find the car. A car that does not exist cannot be retrieved. In this example: The car is on tray T17 at P17. (found)", "Row 3. The car's node must not be kept out for its size. In this example: P17 is not kept out. (passes)", "Row 4. A car on a charging VECS must stop charging first (chained after the VECS's previous event); a VECS in another busy state means 'try later' (is_retryable). In this example: P17 has no VECS. (skipped)", "Row 5. Choose a bay: walk the layout's bay list from the back, skip unusable bays, take the first one already in retrieve mode, else remember the first one in insert mode or with a car inserted. In this example: Assume the layout prioritises [B7, B21]. Walking from the back: B21 is READY_TO_INSERT, so it is remembered; B7 is disabled and skipped. No bay is READY_TO_RETRIEVE, so B21 is used. (bay = B21)", "Row 6. No usable bay: fail and ask Dispatch to keep the job for later (is_retryable). In this example: A bay was found. (skipped)", "Row 7. If the chosen bay is not in retrieve mode yet, add the transition that switches it, on the layout's retrieve floor (chained to the bay, rule A). In this example: B21 must switch to retrieve mode before trays can go in or out on the garage side. (adds 1)", "Row 8. If a tray already occupies the bay, plan it out of the bay; its destination is left for tray assignment. In this example: Empty tray T21 occupies B21. It must leave first; where it goes is decided later. (adds 2 \u00b7 rule B)", "Row 9. Plan the car's tray into the bay, turned so the car faces the right way. In this example: T17 goes into B21, turned so the car faces the right way for the customer. Inside the call: rule B (after 2) and rule C (after B21's last event, 1). (adds 3 \u00b7 B, C)", "Row 10. Add the hand-over: the bay processes the retrieve once the tray is in. In this example: The bay hands the car over once T17 is inside. (adds 4 \u00b7 A, B)", "Row 11. Report success. In this example: Plan() appends the job to ctx->scheduled_jobs. (success)", "Playing the plan (one illustrative execution: AGV assignment and motion planning choose the real AGV and route): event 1. B21 switches to READY_TO_RETRIEVE.", "Playing the plan: AGV-1 drives empty W11 -> W9 -> W8 -> W13 -> W18 -> W22 -> W41 -> B21 and stops under T21 (the approach for event 2; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: event 2. AGV-1 lifts T21, carries it B21 -> W41 -> W22 -> P23 and lowers it. The destination P23 is illustrative: tray assignment fills the '?' later.", "Playing the plan: AGV-1 drives empty P23 -> P19 -> P15 and stops under T15 (the approach for moving T15; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: blocker. T15 stands in the way of event 3: AGV-1 lifts T15, carries it P15 -> P19 and lowers it. P19 is illustrative: this blocker move is added later by tray assignment (ResolveBlockingTrays), not by the job method.", "Playing the plan: AGV-1 drives empty P19 -> P15 -> P17 and stops under T17 (the approach for event 3; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: event 3. AGV-1 lifts T17, carries it P17 -> P15 -> W13 -> W18 -> W22 -> W41 -> B21 and lowers it.", "Playing the plan: event 4. B21 processes the retrieve: the car is handed to the customer. Every tray and AGV is now where the plan leaves it."]
